[Thinking]
**Drafting Shipping Notification Alternatives**

I'm currently exploring various phrasing and tones for communicating shipping delays. My focus is on crafting clear, empathetic, and actionable messages for customers, aiming to offer multiple options that suit different business styles and situations.

**Refining Delay Notification Options**

I'm now focusing on developing distinct notification templates for various delay scenarios. This includes a standard polite version, one for unforeseen external issues, an apologetic one with compensation for significant delays, and a concise SMS option.
[/Thinking]

Here are a few templates you can use to inform a customer about a delayed delivery. Choose the one that best fits your situation (whether it's a minor delay, a major issue, or out of your control). 

### Option 1: Standard / General Delay (Best for minor delays)
**Subject:** Update on your order: #[Order Number] is experiencing a slight delay

Dear [Customer Name],

We are writing to let you know that there is a slight delay with your recent order (#[Order Number]). 

While we always aim to deliver your items as quickly as possible, our courier has informed us that your package is taking a little longer than expected to arrive. 

Your new estimated delivery date is between **[Date]** and **[Date]**. 

You can continue to monitor your package’s journey using your tracking link here: [Insert Tracking Link]

We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience and appreciate your patience. If you have any questions or concerns, please reply directly to this email and we will be happy to help.

Best regards,

[Your Name/Company Name] 

***

### Option 2: Unforeseen Circumstances (Weather, strikes, customs, etc.)
**Subject:** Important update regarding your delivery: Order #[Order Number]

Dear [Customer Name],

Thank you for shopping with [Company Name]. We are reaching out to provide an update on your order #[Order Number].

Unfortunately, due to [unforeseen weather conditions / a courier strike / high volume at customs / unexpected carrier delays], your delivery has been delayed. 

Please be assured that your package is safely on its way, but it will arrive later than our original estimate of [Original Delivery Date]. We now expect your order to arrive by **[New Estimated Date]**.

Track your order anytime here: [Insert Tracking Link]

We understand that waiting for a package is frustrating, and we apologize that this situation has impacted your delivery. Thank you for your continued patience and understanding. 

Warmly,

[Your Name/Company Name]

***

### Option 3: Major Delay + Offering Compensation (Best for retaining unhappy customers)
**Subject:** We sincerely apologize – Update on your order #[Order Number]

Dear [Customer Name],

We are contacting you because your order #[Order Number] has been significantly delayed. We know you were expecting your items by [Original Date], and we are so sorry that we have missed that mark. 

Currently, your package is [explain briefly, e.g., held up at the courier sorting facility], and your new estimated delivery date is **[New Date]**. You can track its progress here: [Insert Tracking Link].

We know this is incredibly frustrating, and we hold ourselves to a higher standard. To make up for this inconvenience, [please accept this promo code for X% off your next order: PROMOCODE / we have refunded your shipping costs to your original payment method]. 

If you need this item urgently and can no longer wait, please let us know so we can discuss alternative solutions or process a cancellation. 

Thank you for your patience and for being a valued customer. 

Best regards,

[Your Name/Company Name]
[Contact Information]

***

### Option 4: Short SMS / Text Message Template
Hi [Customer Name]. Your [Company Name] order #[Order Number] is taking a little longer than expected. Your new estimated delivery date is [New Date]. Track your package here: [Tracking Link]. We apologize for the delay! Reply to this text if you have any questions.

***

**Tips before sending:**
*   Always include the **Order Number** in the subject line.
*   Make sure the **Tracking Link** is clickable.
*   Don't over-explain or make too many excuses; focus on the *solution* and the *new timeline*.
